messages:
pagerduty: Paging on-call: Severity=2 - sustained p99 latency spike for /v1/generate (streaming). Pager: sam
incident-bot: Alert triggered: p99 > 1.2s for route=stream.generate, env=prod, metric=latency_stream_p99, since=3m :rotating_light:
sam: Oncall sam here, grabbing it. Any customer-facing impact yet?
ashley: Support - seeing 3 customer telemetry alerts (trial orgs) complaining about long streaming stalls. No errors returned, connections stay open.
neha: Looking at infra metrics — one GPU host gnode-58 shows high ECC corrected error rate and GPU clock throttle events. Temperature peaked at 96C around spike window.
kai: Runtime: streaming runtime reports many stalled chunk sends; backend logs show repeated kernel timeouts + nvlink recoveries. gpu-node gnode-58 has been bouncing between active and throttle.
sam: Can we reroute off that host immediately? Add it to drain pool and redirect new sessions.
kai: Doing it now. Running: `kubectl label nodes gnode-58 maintenance=true && redwoodctl route update --exclude-node gnode-58`
neha: Also kicking an immediate evict on long-lived sessions: `redwoodctl sessions evict --node gnode-58 --grace=10s` — this will force reconnects to healthy nodes.
incident-bot: Action logged: node gnode-58 set to maintenance by kai at 1912346020.
ashley: Notifying the affected customers with a short blurb. Draft: "We're investigating elevated streaming latency. You may see delayed streaming responses; we're rerouting workloads. Will update in 15m."
sam: Ops checklist: 1) drain gnode-58 2) route traffic away 3) spin up +2 hot GPUs to absorb load 4) enable streaming fallback (chunked flush) 5) update status page
kai: Autoscaling +2 nodes requested: `redwoodctl scale pool hot +2 --reason "incident 1912345678"` — pods are coming up in us-west-2.
neha: Captured kernel logs from gnode-58: ```[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:06:00): 31, PID 1234, GPU failure during command submission``` also series of `GPU: Thermal limit reached` messages.
sam: Given corrected ECC errors, do we suspect a flaky GPU rather than infra config?
neha: Corrected ECCs spiked then thermal throttle followed. Could be degraded HBM module + insufficient cooling on that rack.
kai: For immediate customer safety, enable model-variant fallback for streaming routes: `routing.rule add --route /v1/generate --fallback-model small-q8 --condition streaming` this reduces memory pressure and should avoid long kv-cache runs.
maria: I'll own customer comms and status page. Updating: "Investigating latency: streaming degraded due to GPU hardware degradation; traffic being routed away; mitigation in progress."
ashley: Which SLAs affected? p95 is OK; p99 and streaming SLO breached for ~4m. We should note timeframe.
sam: Good to record: p99 spike window 1912345900 - 1912346200 (~5min), affected multi-tenant streaming sessions ~0.1% of production traffic.
kai: All new sessions are avoiding gnode-58. Draining complete at 1912346400. Evicted sessions reconnected to healthy nodes.
neha: I'm running a forced reboot on gnode-58 for deeper diag, will collect nvram logs and ship to hw team: `sudo reboot && /usr/local/bin/dump-nvlogs.sh > /tmp/gnode58-nvlog.tgz`
incident-bot: Incident update: mitigation applied — traffic rerouted, node drained, autoscale +2 in place.
maria: Status page updated. Customers notified.
sam: Monitoring shows p99 returning to baseline, streaming chunk rate normalized. Can we keep gnode-58 offline pending hardware replacement?
neha: Yes hold offline. Mark as suspect HW. I will open a hardware replacement ticket with rack and serial details.
ashley: Support: pushing a follow-up email to impacted customers summarizing root-cause hypothesis and next steps.
kai: Follow-up temporary tuning: lowered streaming prefetch window and tightened KV cache eviction to reduce memory pressure during degraded hardware. Command: `redwoodctl tuning set --service streaming --prefetch 2 --kv-evict-threshold 0.6`
sam: Good. Let's wrap up timeline and owners for postmortem. Maria owns customer comms & status. Neha owns HW RCA and replacement. Kai owns runtime mitigations and long-term fallback automation. I'll own postmortem doc & SLA impact calc.
maria: I'll schedule a postmortem review for tomorrow 10:00 PT and assign initial notes to the incident doc.
incident-bot: Incident resolved: active mitigation complete, system stabilized at 1912346990. Please add runbook gaps if any.
sam: Thanks all — great coordination. We'll follow with RCA and hardware remediation. :thumbsup:
